evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events
report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.reasoning: Mission purpose, users and rationale are clear and referenced, but no explicit measurable mission requirements are stated, so not complete.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.
This research will be ongoing throughout almost the entire design process

criteria.reasoning: Gantt/timetable and task descriptions show a feasible plan, but contingency provisions and planned information sources are limited or absent.

evidence.quote: geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km

criteria.reasoning: Only tutorial/background progress is shown; no preliminary design results or calculations. The orbit statement is technically incorrect.

evidence.quote: Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue.

criteria.reasoning: Readable structure and headings; Gantt is clear but uncaptioned, and references are footnotes/URLs without a full reference list.

technical_issues.issue: States a geostationary orbit at 600 km; GEO altitude is about 35,786 km and 600 km is LEO, so it would not stay fixed over the reef.
No quantified mission requirements such as revisit time, spatial resolution, spectral bands, data latency, coverage or lifetime.
Project plan lacks explicit contingency provisions and planned information sources for launch, orbit and design.
Gantt chart deadlines are unclear; text mentions red deadline lines but chart appears to show only one red line.
STK design starts late in the Gantt chart while the text says simulations will be used throughout.

overall: Mission rationale is strong and referenced, but requirements are not quantified. Plan is feasible yet lacks contingency/sources. Technical progress is minimal and orbit reasoning is wrong. Presentation is readable but references and figure captions are incomplete.
